PullRequest.Title: sessions: Gate promoted new chat action behind experiment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Follow up to #336469 by placing the session-row action swap behind the `sessions.promoteNewChatAction` assignment variable.

- keep Pin or Unpin as the default inline session-row action
- promote New Chat before Archive or Mark as Done only for the treatment group
- keep New Chat and Pin or Unpin available from the context menu
- refresh the treatment when assignments change and cancel stale resolutions
- keep accessibility help aligned with the active experiment variant

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- 178 focused Sessions tests
- targeted ESLint
- client type-check

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup and UI restoration initializes the session-row experiment contribution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockRestore constructor runs synchronously before UI restoration, but it only binds a context key, registers a listener, creates a cancellation source, and starts resolveTreatment without awaiting it. Treatment resolution and its network/cache dependency continue asynchronously and do not block contribution construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the shared TAS client and perform its initial assignment fetches
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared TAS client setup per window (with provider-configured initial endpoint fetches), not one request per treatment name
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: NewSessionActionViewItemContribution was already registered immediately before this contribution at BlockRestore and already injected IWorkbenchAssignmentService, causing the same shared client setup and initial fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client initialization is asynchronous; the new contribution does not await resolveTreatment during BlockRestore

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit tasClientReadTreatmentComplete telemetry after resolving the new treatment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small event for the added startup treatment read
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This specific treatment-read telemetry event did not exist, although the adjacent existing contribution already emitted treatment-read events for its experiments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after asynchronous treatment resolution and is not awaited by BlockRestore

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per Agents window startup; independent of session count. The existing NewSessionActionViewItemContribution in the same BlockRestore phase already instantiates the shared assignment service before this added contribution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One new treatment resolution is started at construction. The shared assignment service owns a single TAS client; the contribution's MutableDisposable cancels its previous consumer before any later resolution starts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WorkbenchAssignmentService shares one TAS client and reads persisted/cached treatment values while initial fetch is pending. Warm treatment reads use the initialized client synchronously behind the promise; the added lookup does not create a per-feature network fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor ordering, delayed singleton sharing, asynchronous invocation, and assignment-service cache/network behavior are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact TAS endpoint count and latency depend on account entitlement and product configuration, but they are shared initialization costs already present before this diff. The only added work is one cached lookup and one small telemetry event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds constant, non-blocking startup work and does not introduce or multiply the TAS network boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Assignment updates refresh the promoted-action treatment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After WorkbenchAssignmentService has completed a refetch and emits onDidRefetchAssignments, the contribution reads one treatment and updates one context key. This is not on user input, rendering, or startup restoration's synchronous critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh TAS assignments before notifying listeners
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared refetch per assignment-service trigger, serving all treatment consumers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assignment service and existing consumers already performed the shared refetch; the diff only subscribes an additional cached treatment read after notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network operation precedes the event consumed by this contribution; the changed listener does not initiate another refetch

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit treatment-read telemetry for the refreshed value
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small event per assignment-change notification that reaches this listener
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No telemetry query existed for sessions.promoteNewChatAction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on a direct user interaction path and does not delay the assignment refetch completion for other consumers

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One treatment lookup per assignment-change event, independent of the number of sessions. Events are assignment/filter/configuration changes rather than row-level events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each event replaces the prior MutableDisposable and cancels the stale race consumer. The underlying shared assignment lookup may finish, but stale results cannot update the context key; there is no per-session fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The post-refetch read uses the already initialized shared TAS client and current assignments. There is no separate cache owned by the contribution and no miss loop or negative-cache retry per row.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event subscription, cancellation/replacement, and the shared cached getTreatment path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The precise frequency of upstream assignment-context events is product-dependent, but the changed work remains constant per event and is not multiplied by sessions or menu instances.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: stale consumers are canceled, work is constant per infrequent assignment update, and no new network fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering visible session rows and switching their primary toolbar action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each rendered row owns a MenuWorkbenchToolBar scoped to that row. When the global experiment context key changes, affected visible toolbars reevaluate menu expressions and replace the Pin/Unpin or New Chat action.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with the number of currently rendered/virtualized row templates, not the total session history. It occurs when the resolved experiment value changes, not on scroll, pointer movement, or every row render beyond ordinary menu evaluation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Context-key notifications are synchronous menu invalidations, but only instantiated/rendered row toolbars are listeners; there is no asynchronous concurrency or boundary call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu metadata is registered once. Context expressions read the global experiment key plus existing row-scoped keys; no cache is added or defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SessionItemRenderer creates one scoped MenuWorkbenchToolBar per rendered template, and MenuImpl listens only to relevant context-key changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously rendered rows depends on viewport size, but realistic cardinality is bounded by virtualization and updates are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the intended one-time/infrequent action swap causes bounded toolbar reevaluation and adds no I/O, IPC, layout read, or unbounded retained state.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideContent synchronously reads the experiment context key and selects one localized sentence while assembling the existing help text.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work independent of session count and chat history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single invocation per accessibility-help request; no queue, parallel work, or repeated asynchronous task.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads the already-resolved context key; no network/cache lookup is performed from accessibility help.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed provider code has no transitive service call beyond IContextKeyService.getValue.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added operation is one context-key lookup and conditional selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a session row context menu or invoking Pin, Unpin, or New Chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu opening evaluates the registered context expressions. The diff changes which existing command appears inline versus in the context menu; command implementations and their service boundaries are unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per menu open or command invocation; selected-session handling remains unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One menu construction per user invocation; action execution remains one selected command with no added parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing menu registration and context-key state; no new data fetch or cache layer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed hunks only alter menu when clauses and registration locations, not action run methods.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the changed mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes action visibility but does not add work to command execution.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced startup, assignment refresh, row rendering/menu invalidation, accessibility help, and action invocation. The only new recurring work is one shared cached treatment lookup plus a small telemetry event per startup/refetch; it is not per session, does not add a network request, and stale resolutions are canceled. No actionable performance finding was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
